sentences: Today we install AWX the way the project recommends: with the AWX Operator on Kubernetes.
We'll use K three S, a one-command Kubernetes, on a single virtual machine.
By the end, you'll log in to your own AWX.
And I'll show you three problems I hit, so you don't lose a night to them.
First, the virtual machine. In VirtualBox I give it four CPUs, eight gigabytes of RAM, and a sixty gigabyte disk.
Network adapter one is host-only, so your PC can reach AWX. Adapter two uses network address translation, for internet access.
One thing on Windows: turn the Windows hypervisor off first.
With it on, VirtualBox runs in Hyper-V mode, you'll see a green turtle icon, and my guest crashed.
Now log in as root and check the machine.
The minimums are two CPUs, four gigabytes of free memory, and fifteen gigabytes of free disk.
Read your own numbers out loud before you go on.
Next, the firewall and S E Linux, if they're turned on.
The Kubernetes API uses port six four four three. AWX itself will listen on port three zero zero eight zero.
The two ten-dot ranges are the pod and service networks.
Permissive S E Linux is a lab shortcut. In production, you'd use the K three S S E Linux policy instead.
Now K three S. It's a full Kubernetes in one binary, installed with one command.
Two flags matter: one skips the S E Linux package, and one makes the Kubernetes config file readable.
Then we wait until the node shows Ready.
Next, the AWX Operator. An operator is a controller that installs AWX from a short YAML file, and keeps it healthy.
Our kustomize file pulls AWX Operator version two point nineteen point one.
Look at the last block. It replaces the proxy image. The old copy is gone, and without this line the operator never starts. That's the first of the three traps.
Then we apply it with kube control apply, dash k.
Now AWX itself. A few short lines describe the whole thing: a name, and the port it listens on, three zero zero eight zero.
Apply it, and the operator does the rest.
Now watch the containers come up one by one. Postgres is the database.
Web is the UI and the API.
The migration step builds the database schema.
Last, the task pod. It's the one that runs your jobs.
This takes about ten minutes, mostly image downloads, so go get a coffee.
When it's ready, one command prints the admin password.
Open your browser at your VM's IP address, port three zero zero eight zero, and log in as admin.
Then change the password right away, from the user menu, under Edit.
Now, the three traps. One: Hyper-V mode crashes the VM. Turn the Windows hypervisor off, and reboot.
Two: the old registry image is gone. Swap in a new one in the kustomize file.
Three: a crash can corrupt downloaded images. Remove the image with C R I C T L, R M I, then let it pull again.
That's a working AWX on K three S.
